tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

2 3 # fast-ulysses 4 5 **Ulysses sequence-parallel all-to-all as a torch custom op, moved by the GPU copy engines.** 6 7 [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) 8 9
10 11 Ulysses sequence parallelism shards a long sequence across GPUs: one all-to-all before attention 12 trades the sequence shard for a head shard, a second trades it back. For long-sequence video DiT 13 workloads those two collectives are the critical communication. 14 15 This ships that 4D all-to-all as `torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d`, over NVLink, on one node. 16 17 ## Key features 18 19 - **No SMs.** The peer transfers are pitched `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` straight into peers' 20 symmetric-memory addresses, so they run on the copy engines while compute kernels hold every SM. 21 (Measured: a peer copy overlaps a concurrent GEMM completely; a same-device copy does not, which 22 is why `out=` from `empty_output()` — which removes the copy-out — is the faster path.) 23 - **Relayout for free.** The sequence/head permutation is expressed as source and destination 24 strides on those copies, not as two permute kernels. That is roughly half of what the 25 `torch.distributed` path spends. 26 - **Uneven shards.** Per-rank `seq_splits` / `head_splits`, which is what lets a caller drop 27 sequence padding. Even splits are the special case, not a separate path. 28 29 ## Performance 30 31 8 GPUs, one exclusively allocated node per row, the same wheel and the same `.so` on all of them. 32 `base` is `torch.distributed` permute + `all_to_all_single` + permute. Wan 720p, bf16, ms. 33 34 | GPU | fabric | base | ours | vs base | transfer | of the fabric | 35 |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| 36 | H200 | NVLink | 1.569 | **0.860** | **1.82×** | 0.680 | 99% | 37 | B200 | NVLink | 1.194 | **0.550** | **2.17×** | 0.410 | 90% | 38 | B300 | NVLink | 1.184 | **0.548** | **2.16×** | 0.411 | 90% | 39 | H100 | NVLink | 1.616 | **0.971** | **1.66×** | 0.715 | 94% | 40 41 47–60% of the baseline is relayout that costs nothing here. "Of the fabric" is the transfer against 42 what a flat peer copy achieves on the same machine — at 90–99% there is nothing left to schedule. 43 `out=` from `empty_output()` removes the copy-out for a further 1.14–1.28×. 44 45 Every number was taken twice, on two different nodes except H100, whose two samples are the same 46 node. Full tables, per-stage timings and the method: [docs/benchmark.md](docs/benchmark.md). 47 48 ## Quick start 49 50 Save this as `example.py` and run `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 example.py`: 51 52 ```python 53 import os 54 55 import torch 56 import torch.distributed as dist 57 from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup 58 59 dist.init_process_group("nccl") 60 torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])) 61 group = UlyssesGroup() 62 63 b, s_local, heads, d = 1, 4096, 8, 128 64 ws = dist.get_world_size() 65 x = torch.randn(b, s_local, heads * ws, d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") 66 67 y = group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0) # (b, s_local * ws, heads, d) 68 z = group.all_to_all_4d(y, mode=1) # back to x's shape 69 70 group.destroy() 71 dist.destroy_process_group() 72 ``` 73 74 Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. More: [docs/quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md). 75 76 A real one — a DiT attention block, sequence-parallel, forward and backward, checked against the 77 same block without sequence parallelism: 78 79 ```bash 80 torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 examples/dit_attention.py 81 ``` 82 83 The collective is differentiable, so that block is an ordinary `nn.Module`: no `autograd.Function` 84 wrapper, no manual backward. 85 86 ## API 87 88 | Entry point | Purpose | 89 | --- | --- | 90 | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=None, device=None, *, require_nvlink=True)` | Collective. Refuses a group whose GPUs are not NVLink-joined. | 91 | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, *, mode=0, out=None, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None)` | The collective. Returns a tensor the caller owns. | 92 | `group.all_to_all_4d_async(x, *, ...)` | The same, on a comm stream, returning an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`. `lend=True` drops the copy-out without a buffer of your own, bounded at 4 live results. | 93 | `group.empty_output(x, *, mode=0, ...)` | A symmetric buffer to pass as `out=`, which removes the copy-out. `out=` gives up the gradient. | 94 | `group.destroy()` | Release the windows. Collective. | 95 | `fast-ulysses doctor` | Build, devices, NVLink matrix. | 96 97 Shapes, splits and the collective contract: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md). Why the code is shaped 98 this way, and what it rests on that is not guaranteed: [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). Coming from 99 DeepSpeed-Ulysses, sglang's `usp.py` or yunchang — what each call becomes, and what this does not 100 have: [docs/migration.md](docs/migration.md). 101 102 ## Limits 103 104 - **NVLink, one node, `world_size` in [1, 8]**, including odd sizes. Over PCIe — especially across 105 a CPU socket — `torch.distributed` is faster, because the pitched copies this transport is built 106 on degrade badly there. The constructor refuses such a group. 107 - `float16` / `bfloat16` / `float32` / `float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2` / `int8` / `uint8`, and 108 `d * elem_size` must be 16-byte aligned — so `d % 8` at bfloat16, `d % 16` at float8. 109 - Differentiable, and it propagates shapes under `FakeTensor`. Not traceable by `torch.compile`: 110 the group is a torchbind object with no registered fake class, so Dynamo graph-breaks on it. 111 - Forward-mode AD works — `torch.autograd.forward_ad`, `torch.func.jvp`, `torch.func.linearize` — 112 at one extra collective for the tangent. Reverse-mode `torch.func` does not: `grad` / `vjp` / 113 `jacrev` raise, and `vmap` raises by an explicit check, since it would run one collective per 114 batch element and ranks that disagree on the batch size hang. 115 - The **async** form is not differentiable and says so: its `AsyncCollectiveTensor` is a leaf, so a 116 gradient would be dropped silently. Use `all_to_all_4d` when you need one. 117 - **`out=` is not differentiable either**, and cannot say so: it reaches a mutating op with no 118 autograd formula, so the result is the caller's buffer, detached. It is a speed knob for 119 inference and no-grad regions, not for a training graph. 120 - CUDA-graph capture covers the sync call on an already-warmed shape; see 121 [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). 122 123 ## Install 124 125 Requires **PyTorch 2.10+**, **CUDA 12.8+ or 13**, and sm80 / sm90 / sm100 / sm120. torch is the 126 only runtime dependency. 127 128 A wheel is built against one (torch minor, CUDA major) and embeds that torch's C++ ABI, so the pair 129 has to match. Install torch first, then pick the index by the CUDA major it was built against: 130 131 ```bash 132 pip install fast-ulysses --index-url https://triple-mu.github.io/fast-ulysses/whl/cu13/ # or cu12 133 ``` 134 135 That index carries fast-ulysses and nothing else, so pip cannot move your torch to satisfy it: it 136 backtracks to the wheel pinned to the torch minor you already have. `fast-ulysses wheel-url` names 137 the row for the environment running now and prints the same install as a fully pinned 138 `--find-links` command against the release assets, when you want the file itself. 139 140 ```bash 141 pip install fast-ulysses # PyPI: torch 2.13.x + CUDA 13 142 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation # from source, all four arches 143 FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH=90 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation # one arch, much faster 144 ``` 145 146 PyPI carries that one pair, pinned `torch==2.13.*`. On any other torch the first command does not 147 fail — pip upgrades torch to 2.13, a different CUDA build than the one you chose. 148 149 The one thing to know before reaching for `--find-links`: PEP 440 orders local versions, so an 150 install that does not write `+torch210cu128` out in full takes `torch213cu130` whatever torch you 151 have, silently. That, the per-row indexes and what to do when the import fails: 152 [docs/install.md](docs/install.md). 153 154 ## Testing 155 156 ```bash 157 pytest # the host-only plan tests always run; the GPU workers skip below 2 GPUs 158 pytest -m "not multigpu" # host-only, no GPU needed 159 torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 test/distributed/correctness.py 160 ``` 161 162 Development setup: [docs/develop.md](docs/develop.md). 163 164 ## License 165 166 Apache-2.0. 1	# Installation
2	
3	## Requirements
4	
5	- **PyTorch 2.10+**, Linux x86_64, CPython 3.10–3.13
6	- **CUDA 12.8+ or 13**
7	- sm80 / sm90 / sm100 / sm120, NVLink-joined
8	- For a source build only: CMake ≥ 3.18 and `nvcc`. `ccache` is used when present.
9	
10	torch is the only runtime dependency. Windows come from `c10d::symmetric_memory`, and the floor is
11	`get_signal_pad_size()`, which becomes a free `TORCH_API` function in torch 2.10 — that is what the
12	handshake's placement in the pad is computed from. `empty_strided_p2p` and `rendezvous` themselves
13	go back further. CUDA 12.6 and below cannot emit `sm_100` / `sm_120`.
14	
15	## Install
16	
17	A release is 36 wheels: 8 (torch minor, CUDA major) rows × 4 CPythons, plus 4 untagged ones for
18	PyPI. The torch minor must match exactly and the CUDA major must match, because the extension
19	embeds `c10d::Work` vtables, a pybind11 module and a `TORCH_LIBRARY` registration, none of which
20	survive a minor bump. Which row you are:
21	
22	```bash
23	python -c "import sys,torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, sys.version_info[:2])"
24	```
25	
26	| your torch | torch's CUDA | wheel tag |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| 2.10.x | 12.x | `torch210cu128` |
29	| 2.10.x | 13.x | `torch210cu130` |
30	| 2.11.x | 12.x | `torch211cu128` |
31	| 2.11.x | 13.x | `torch211cu130` |
32	| 2.12.x | 12.x | `torch212cu129` |
33	| 2.12.x | 13.x | `torch212cu130` |
34	| 2.13.x | 12.x | `torch213cu129` |
35	| 2.13.x | 13.x | `torch213cu130` |
36	
37	The tag is the wheel's PEP 440 local version — `fast_ulysses-0.2.0+torch210cu128-cp312-…` — which
38	is what you write after `==` when you name one. The index picks it for you.
39	
40	### From the index
41	
42	```bash
43	pip install fast-ulysses --index-url https://triple-mu.github.io/fast-ulysses/whl/cu13/
44	```
45	
46	Two indexes, `cu12` and `cu13`, picked by the major of `torch.version.cuda`; `cu128`, `cu129` and
47	`cu130` are aliases holding the same wheels, since that suffix is what you read off the URL your
48	torch came from. The CUDA major is chosen by URL because no wheel metadata records it, the same
49	reason `download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128` is laid out that way.
50	
51	The torch minor is not chosen, it is resolved. An index carries fast-ulysses and nothing else, so
52	pip cannot install a torch to satisfy its first candidate — `0.2.0+torch213cu130`, the highest
53	local version there — and backtracks until it reaches the one whose `Requires-Dist: torch==2.11.*`
54	the installed torch already satisfies.
55	
56	Install torch first. With no torch installed nothing satisfies any candidate, and the install ends
57	on `ResolutionImpossible` after listing every row it tried:
58	
59	```
60	ERROR: Cannot install fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu130, ... because these package versions have
61	conflicting dependencies.
62	The conflict is caused by:
63	    fast-ulysses 0.2.0+torch213cu130 depends on torch==2.13.*
64	    ...
65	```
66	
67	The rows do not conflict with each other; each of them conflicts with the torch that is not there.
68	That is the intended failure — nothing here resolves torch for you — and `pip install torch` first
69	is the whole of the fix.
70	
71	Do not add `--extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple`. It gives pip a torch to install, so the
72	first candidate resolves after all, by moving your torch to 2.13. Install whatever else needs PyPI
73	in its own command — or use a per-row index, one per tag in the table above:
74	
75	```bash
76	pip install fast-ulysses --index-url https://triple-mu.github.io/fast-ulysses/whl/torch211cu128/
77	```
78	
79	That one holds a single row, four wheels, one per CPython, so there is nothing for pip to choose
80	between and no other index can outbid it. It is the form to use when something else in the same
81	command must come from PyPI. It follows its row across releases: when a row's CUDA *minor* moves —
82	2.12 went `cu128` → `cu129` — the index named after the old one keeps receiving that row's wheels,
83	so a URL written down once keeps resolving. The CUDA major never moves that way; it is what the
84	name promises.
85	
86	The indexes cover 0.2.0 and later. For 0.1.0, use `--find-links` on that release.
87	
88	### From the release, by hand or by `wheel-url`
89	
90	```bash
91	fast-ulysses wheel-url
92	```
93	
94	reports the row for the torch, CUDA, python and machine running now, and prints the command for
95	it, with the version written out in full:
96	
97	```bash
98	pip install "fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu128" \
99	  --find-links https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/releases/expanded_assets/v0.2.0
100	```
101	
102	`--find-links` on `expanded_assets` rather than a constructed asset URL: the file name carries
103	whatever platform tag auditwheel compressed to — v0.1.0 shipped
104	`manylinux_2_24_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64` — so writing the name out is a guess. That endpoint
105	is the fragment the release page loads its asset list from, and it lists all 36. The page itself,
106	<https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/releases/tag/v0.2.0>, carries no `.whl` link and answers
107	`Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement` for every version. GitHub documents
108	neither endpoint. `SHA256SUMS` on the release covers every file.
109	
110	`wheel-url` needs an extension that loads: it is a subcommand of the `fast-ulysses` script, which
111	imports the package, which imports `_C`. When `_C` is what is broken, the import error itself
112	already names both sides — see [When the import fails](#when-the-import-fails).
113	
114	### From PyPI — torch 2.13.x and CUDA 13 only
115	
116	```bash
117	pip install fast-ulysses
118	```
119	
120	PyPI rejects PEP 440 local versions, so exactly one row goes there: `torch213cu130`, with the tag
121	stripped. Its metadata is `Requires-Dist: torch==2.13.*`. **On any other torch this command does
122	not fail.** pip satisfies that pin by upgrading torch to 2.13 from PyPI — a different torch and a
123	different CUDA build than the one you installed — and reports it as an ordinary dependency
124	resolution. Use the index, or the command `wheel-url` prints, for every other row.
125	
126	### The version must be written out in full
127	
128	Under PEP 440 a local label is compared segment by segment, and a specifier without one ignores
129	the label entirely, so `==0.2.0` matches all nine artifacts of 0.2.0 and the highest wins:
130	
131	```
132	0.2.0 < +torch210cu128 < +torch210cu130 < +torch211cu128 < +torch211cu130
133	      < +torch212cu129 < +torch212cu130 < +torch213cu129 < +torch213cu130
134	```
135	
136	Over any file set holding more than one row — `--find-links`, `--extra-index-url`, a directory of
137	downloaded wheels — an unqualified requirement therefore takes `torch213cu130` whatever torch is
138	installed, silently:
139	
140	```bash
141	# ./wheelhouse holding all 36
142	pip install fast-ulysses --find-links ./wheelhouse                       # -> +torch213cu130
143	pip install "fast-ulysses==0.2.0" --find-links ./wheelhouse              # -> +torch213cu130
144	pip install "fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu128" --find-links ./wheelhouse   # -> only that one
145	```
146	
147	So with `--find-links` or `--extra-index-url`, write the label out; `--index-url` at `whl/cu12` or
148	`whl/cu13` needs no label because the torch pin resolves the row there, and `whl/<tag>` needs none
149	because there is only the one row in it — that is the one that also holds up beside PyPI. The
150	written-out label is also the form that does not depend on index priority: pip unions every index
151	and takes the highest version, `uv pip install` defaults to `first-index` and stops at the first
152	index carrying the project, and an exact version survives both.
153	
154	One more thing pip does not do here: replace an installation it already has. `pip install
155	fast-ulysses` with any version present prints `Requirement already satisfied` and leaves the wrong
156	row in place — `--upgrade` does not help either, since the row it would upgrade to is the highest
157	one. Uninstall first, or name the version in full.
158	
159	### For a torch the table does not list
160	
161	```bash
162	pip install fast-ulysses --no-binary fast-ulysses --no-build-isolation
163	```
164	
165	The sdist compiles against the torch already installed. `--no-build-isolation` is required for the
166	reason in the next section; without it the build stops with that instruction rather than a
167	traceback.
168	
169	## Build from source
170	
171	```bash
172	pip install -e . --no-build-isolation                              # all four architectures
173	FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH=90 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation    # one, much faster
174	```
175	
176	`--no-build-isolation` is required: CMake locates libtorch through the installed torch, so torch
177	has to be importable at build time, and it must be the one you intend to run against.
178	
179	| Variable | Meaning |
180	| --- | --- |
181	| `FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH` | Target compute capabilities, `;`-separated. Default `80;90;100;120`. |
182	| `CUDACXX` | CUDA compiler; defaults to `/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc`. |
183	| `FAST_ULYSSES_BUILD_DIR` | CMake build tree. Default `./build`, kept between builds so rebuilds are incremental. |
184	| `FAST_ULYSSES_CMAKE_ARGS` | Extra flags passed through to CMake. |
185	| `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL` | Overrides the job count, which is otherwise bounded by available memory rather than core count. |
186	
187	## When the import fails
188	
189	`import fast_ulysses` catches the loader error and reports what the extension was built against
190	next to what is installed. The `fast-ulysses` script imports the same package, so it raises the
191	same report instead of running — `doctor`'s devices and NVLink matrix need a load that works. The
192	two common causes:
193	
194	- **`undefined symbol: _ZN3c10...`** — the wheel's torch minor is not the installed torch's. Either
195	  the wrong row was installed, or torch moved after it: the plain `pip install fast-ulysses` moves
196	  torch to 2.13 itself, and reinstalling the torch you wanted afterwards leaves exactly this.
197	- **`libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file`** — a CUDA-12 wheel in a CUDA-13 environment
198	  or the reverse. No `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` fixes this.
199	
200	Both are the same repair, and the import error has already printed the two sides of it, so it needs
201	neither the table nor a working extension:
202	
203	```bash
204	python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda)"   # the torch you chose?
205	pip uninstall -y fast-ulysses
206	pip install fast-ulysses --index-url https://triple-mu.github.io/fast-ulysses/whl/cu13/
207	```
208	
209	Check torch first, in that order. If it is not the torch you installed, an earlier
210	`pip install fast-ulysses` moved it (see PyPI, above); reinstall the torch you want before this, or
211	you pin the row you were moved to. The uninstall is not optional — without it pip reports
212	`Requirement already satisfied` and the broken wheel stays. Naming the version in full,
213	`pip install "fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu128" --find-links …`, replaces it in one command.
214	
215	## When the group will not build
216	
217	- **`cuda:i and cuda:j are not joined by NVLink`** — the constructor's check. Use
218	  `torch.distributed` on that machine; over PCIe, and especially across a CPU socket, it is faster
219	  than this transport. `require_nvlink=False` builds the group anyway, for measuring that case.
220	- **`NVML could not report the link topology`** (from `doctor`) — the check cannot answer, so it
221	  does not refuse. Nothing is claimed either way.
222	
223	## Other problems
224	
225	- **NCCL dies at init with `unhandled cuda error` / "Failed to bind NVLink SHARP (NVLS) Multicast
226	  memory"** — a Fabric Manager or NVSwitch configuration problem on that machine. Run with
227	  `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`. This affects the `torch.distributed` bootstrap, not this operator.
228	- **`CUDASymmetricMemory.cu: ... init_multicast_for_block` warnings, then "Gracefully skipping
229	  multicast initialization"** — the same machines, the same cause, printed by torch rather than
230	  NCCL. Harmless here: the multicast path is NVLS, and this transport writes peer addresses
231	  directly and never uses it.
232	- **CMake `CMakeCache.txt directory ... is different than ...`** — the persistent `build/` was
233	  configured from another path (the repo moved). `rm -rf build` and rebuild.

22	def _base_version() -> str:
23	    """The one version literal, read out of ./VERSION.
24	
25	    CMake reads the same file, and setup.py bakes it into _build_meta.py, which is where the
26	    installed package reads __version__ from.

31	def _build_jobs(arch: str) -> int:
32	    """How many translation units to compile at once, bounded by MEMORY, not just cores.
33	
34	    Each job forks one nvcc, and -t0 makes that nvcc run one device pass per architecture at the
35	    same time, so peak concurrency is jobs * len(arch) and peak memory scales with it. A small CI
36	    runner is killed by the OOM reaper partway through a four-architecture build if -j follows the
37	    core count alone. Budget 3 GiB per concurrent pass. Falls back to the core count where
38	    MemAvailable is not readable; CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL overrides either way.
39	    """
40	    cpus = os.cpu_count() or 1
41	    n_arch = max(1, len([a for a in arch.split(";") if a]))
42	    try:
43	        for line in Path("/proc/meminfo").read_text().splitlines():
44	            if line.startswith("MemAvailable:"):
45	                gib = int(line.split()[1]) / (1024 * 1024)
46	                break
47	        else:
48	            return cpus
49	    except OSError:
50	        return cpus
51	    return max(1, min(cpus, int(gib / (3.0 * n_arch))))

67	    build isolation -- and torch cannot be declared a build requirement either, because pip
68	    would then install its own copy into the isolated environment and the extension would link
69	    that one instead of the user's. Turn the bare ModuleNotFoundError into the instruction.
70	    """

72	        import torch

78	            "    pip install fast-ulysses --no-build-isolation\n"
79	            "Prebuilt wheels avoid the source build entirely: see docs/install.md."

"""The ``fast-ulysses`` command: ``doctor`` and ``wheel-url``.

``doctor`` answers whether this machine can run the operator. What decides it is whether every
pair of devices is joined by NVLink, since the transport writes peer memory directly. This reports
what can be established without a process group -- the build, the devices, the NVLink matrix -- so
a green matrix is a necessary condition, not a substitute for the check UlyssesGroup's constructor
makes over the actual group.

``wheel-url`` answers which published wheel matches the torch, CUDA, python and architecture
running right now, and prints the version written out in full, because PEP 440 orders local
versions and a bare requirement therefore resolves to the highest tag rather than to this torch.
docs/install.md has that argument in full.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import platform
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def _load():
    """(module, error). NOT the path a failed import takes when this runs as the console script:
    that imports the package first, so ``_diagnose.explain``'s report is raised before ``main``
    runs -- docs/install.md says so under "When the import fails". What is left for this to catch
    is cli.py run as a file, from a tree where nothing is installed."""
    try:
        import fast_ulysses

        return fast_ulysses, None
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the failure IS the report
        return None, exc


def _doctor() -> int:
    pkg, err = _load()
    if err is not None:
        # Already rendered: fast_ulysses/__init__ routes a load failure through _diagnose.explain
        # before re-raising, and importing _diagnose here would re-run the __init__ that failed.
        print(f"extension: FAILED TO LOAD\n{type(err).__name__}: {err}")
        return 1
    print(f"extension: {pkg._C.__file__}")
    from fast_ulysses._diagnose import build_meta

    for key, value in sorted(build_meta().items()):
        print(f"  {key.lower()}: {value}")

    import torch

    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        print("devices: none visible to CUDA")
        return 1

    n = torch.cuda.device_count()
    # Leading digits only: the arch list carries whatever was asked for, and 90a and 120-real name
    # the same GPUs as 90 and 120. CMakeLists normalises with the same match.
    built = {
        m.group()
        for a in pkg._C.build_info()["cuda_arch_list"].split(",")
        if (m := re.match(r"[0-9]+", a.strip()))
    }
    print(f"devices: {n}")
    for i in range(n):
        p = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i)
        arch = f"{p.major}{p.minor}"
        mark = "" if arch in built else "  <-- NOT IN THIS BUILD"
        print(f"  [{i}] {p.name}  sm_{arch}  {p.total_memory >> 30} GiB{mark}")

    matrix = pkg._C.nvlink_matrix(list(range(n)))
    if matrix is None:
        print("\nNVLink: NVML could not report the link topology on this machine.")
        print("UlyssesGroup will build anyway; nothing here can say whether it should.")
        return 0

    print("\nnvlink, row=from col=to:")
    print("     " + " ".join(f"{j:>3}" for j in range(n)))
    missing = []
    for i in range(n):
        row = []
        for j in range(n):
            ok = matrix[(i, j)]
            row.append(" . " if i == j else (" y " if ok else " N "))
            if i != j and not ok:
                missing.append((i, j))
        print(f"  {i:>2} " + " ".join(row))

    if missing:
        print(
            f"\nNOT NVLink-joined: {len(missing)} pair(s), e.g. {missing[:4]}.\n"
            "A group spanning any of those is refused at construction. Use torch.distributed\n"
            "there: it routes around the link, and this transport does not."
        )
        return 1
    if n < 2:
        # The pair loop above is empty here, and "all 1 devices are joined" is the one sentence a
        # reader takes away from the subcommand.
        print("\none visible device: no pair to check, and nothing above world_size 1 to run")
        return 0
    print(f"\nall {n} devices are mutually NVLink-joined")
    return 0


_MATRIX = Path(__file__).with_name("wheel_matrix.json")

# What to do when no wheel matches. The sdist builds against the torch already installed, which
# is the whole reason it cannot run under pip's build isolation. --no-binary is not optional:
# without it pip takes the untagged PyPI wheel -- which matches any x86_64 cp310-cp313 and pins
# torch==2.13.* -- and moves this torch to 2.13 to satisfy it. That is the failure this whole
# subcommand exists to prevent, and every message below ends on this line.
_FROM_SOURCE = (
    "  pip install fast-ulysses --no-binary fast-ulysses --no-build-isolation   # needs nvcc"
)


def _abi(version: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(major, minor) of a torch version. Ordered as integers, so 2.9 sorts below 2.10."""
    major, minor = version.split(".")[:2]
    return int(major), int(minor)


def _tag(row: dict) -> str:
    """A row's local version, e.g. torch210cu128 -- check_wheel.py parses the inverse form."""
    major, minor = _abi(row["torch"])
    return f"torch{major}{minor}cu{row['cuda'].replace('.', '')}"


def _match(matrix: dict, live: dict[str, str], machine: str) -> dict | str:
    """The published row for this environment, or the text naming the axis that has no wheel.

    The axes are checked in the order they are decided in: architecture and python are the wheel's
    own tags, torch minor and CUDA major are what the .so is pinned to. Matching on the CUDA MAJOR
    and not the minor is deliberate -- the extension links libcudart.so.<major> and nothing else
    from the toolkit, and check_wheel.py asserts exactly that much.
    """
    rows = matrix["rows"]
    if machine != matrix["machine"]:
        return (
            f"no wheel for {machine}: every published wheel is {matrix['platform_tag']}.\n"
            f"options:\n{_FROM_SOURCE}"
        )
    if live["python"] not in matrix["pythons"]:
        return (
            f"no wheel for {live['python']}: the published pythons are "
            f"{', '.join(matrix['pythons'])}.\n"
            f"options:\n  run one of those interpreters, or\n{_FROM_SOURCE}"
        )
    if live["torch"] == "unimportable":
        return (
            "torch does not import here, and its minor and CUDA major are what pick the wheel.\n"
            "Install the torch you intend to run, then run this again."
        )

    abis = sorted({".".join(r["torch"].split(".")[:2]) for r in rows}, key=_abi)
    if live["torch_abi"] not in abis:
        near = abis[0] if _abi(live["torch_abi"]) < _abi(abis[0]) else abis[-1]
        return (
            f"no wheel for torch {live['torch_abi']}: published for torch {', '.join(abis)}.\n"
            "The .so embeds c10d::Work vtables, a pybind11 module and a TORCH_LIBRARY\n"
            "registration, none of which survive a torch minor bump.\n"
            f"options:\n"
            f'  pip install "torch=={near}.*"   # the nearest published torch, then run this '
            f"again\n{_FROM_SOURCE}"
        )

    same = [r for r in rows if ".".join(r["torch"].split(".")[:2]) == live["torch_abi"]]
    majors = sorted({r["cuda"].split(".")[0] for r in same})
    if live["cuda"] in ("None", "unknown"):
        return (
            "no wheel: torch.version.cuda is None, so this is a CPU (or ROCm) build of\n"
            "torch, and every wheel links libcudart.\n"
            f"Install a CUDA {' or '.join(majors)} build of torch {live['torch_abi']}, then run "
            "this again."
        )
    if live["cuda"].split(".")[0] not in majors:
        return (
            f"no wheel for CUDA {live['cuda']}: torch {live['torch_abi']} is published for CUDA "
            f"{' and '.join(majors)}.\n"
            "A CUDA major mismatch fails at import on libcudart, and no LD_LIBRARY_PATH fixes "
            f"it.\noptions:\n{_FROM_SOURCE}"
        )
    return next(r for r in same if r["cuda"].split(".")[0] == live["cuda"].split(".")[0])


def _wheel_url() -> int:
    # Relative, with the flat name as the fallback: `import fast_ulysses` imports torch, and this
    # subcommand has to answer for a torch that is not installed or will not import. Running
    # cli.py as a file is the only way to reach here in that state, and there is no package to be
    # relative to then.
    try:
        from ._diagnose import _live, build_meta
    except ImportError:
        from _diagnose import _live, build_meta

    matrix, live, machine = json.loads(_MATRIX.read_text()), _live(), platform.machine()
    print(f"running: torch {live['torch']}, cuda {live['cuda']}, {live['python']}, {machine}")

    row = _match(matrix, live, machine)
    if isinstance(row, str):
        print(row)
        return 1

    # The base version of THIS package: a release publishes one wheel per row, so the row picked
    # above only names a file within the release this package came from.
    version = str(build_meta().get("VERSION", "")).partition("+")[0]
    if not version:
        print("_build_meta.py is missing, so the release this package came from cannot be named.")
        return 1

    torch_abi = ".".join(row["torch"].split(".")[:2])
    print(
        f"\nrow: torch {torch_abi}, CUDA {row['cuda']}, {live['python']}, {matrix['platform_tag']}"
    )
    if row.get("pypi"):
        print(f"\n  pip install fast-ulysses=={version}\n")
        print(
            "This is the row PyPI carries, and the only one published without a local\n"
            "version: its torch is what a plain `pip install torch` resolves to."
        )
        return 0

    # --find-links, not a constructed asset URL: the filename carries whatever compressed platform
    # tag auditwheel emitted, which nothing here can predict, so naming the file would be a guess.
    # The release PAGE is useless to pip -- its assets are lazy-loaded and its HTML holds no .whl
    # link -- and expanded_assets is the fragment it loads them from, which lists all of them.
    print(
        f'\n  pip install "fast-ulysses=={version}+{_tag(row)}" \\\n'
        f"    --find-links {matrix['find_links'].format(version=version)}\n"
    )
    pypi_row = next(r for r in matrix["rows"] if r.get("pypi"))
    pypi_abi = ".".join(pypi_row["torch"].split(".")[:2])
    print(
        f"The version has to be written out in full. PEP 440 orders local versions, and\n"
        f"{version}+{_tag(pypi_row)} is above every other tag of this release, so both\n"
        f"`pip install fast-ulysses` and `fast-ulysses=={version}` resolve to the torch\n"
        f"{pypi_abi} wheel -- which declares torch=={pypi_abi}.*, so pip would then move this\n"
        f"torch to {pypi_abi} as well. Nothing warns."
    )
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="fast-ulysses")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="report the build, the devices, and the NVLink matrix")
    sub.add_parser("wheel-url", help="the published wheel for this torch, CUDA, python and arch")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "doctor":
        return _doctor()
    if args.command == "wheel-url":
        return _wheel_url()
    parser.error(f"unknown command {args.command}")
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Quick start

## Wrapping attention

The two calls bracket attention: mode 0 trades the sequence shard for a head shard, mode 1 trades
it back.

```python
import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

dist.init_process_group("nccl")
torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
ws = dist.get_world_size()

group = UlyssesGroup()          # collective; refuses a group that is not NVLink-joined

def attention_block(qkv):       # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
    qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)      # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
    out = attention(qkv)                        # each rank now holds whole sequences
    return group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)     # -> (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)
```

Pack q, k and v into one collective when you can: the last dim is just `3 * head_dim`, and one
call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three.

## Removing the copy-out

The default returns a tensor the call allocated, which costs one flat device-to-device copy out of
the window. Give it a symmetric buffer instead and the peers write that buffer directly:

```python
buf = group.empty_output(qkv, mode=0)     # collective: allocate ONCE, outside the loop
for step in range(steps):
    y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, out=buf)   # no copy-out; y is buf
```

`buf` is an ordinary tensor you own. It is overwritten by the next call that uses it, so use one
buffer per concurrent call.

`out=` gives up the gradient: the result comes back with no `grad_fn` and no `requires_grad`, and
nothing raises. Use it in inference and under `torch.no_grad()`; inside a training graph, call
without `out=`.

## Overlapping with compute

The transfer uses no SMs, so it can run underneath compute. Submit it, do the compute, then use the
result — the first aten op on it inserts the wait GPU-side.

```python
y = group.all_to_all_4d_async(qkv, mode=0)   # inference only: raises if qkv requires grad
h = some_gemm_chain(other_input)             # runs while the copy engines move qkv
y = y.wait()                                 # or just use y; the first op waits by itself
```

The async form is not differentiable and refuses a grad-requiring input rather than dropping the
gradient, so in a training step this is the sync call's job.

Wait on, or use, every async result. A dropped one leaves an entry in torch's work registry.

## Dropping the sequence padding

Sharding a sequence usually means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size and padding the
tail, so every rank holds the same length. Those padded tokens then ride through attention and the
collective on every layer of every step. Pass the real per-rank lengths instead:

```python
s = 75827                                    # does not divide by ws
seq_splits = [s // ws + (1 if p < s % ws else 0) for p in range(ws)]
head_splits = [n_global // ws] * ws

y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, seq_splits=seq_splits, head_splits=head_splits)
```

Both lists or neither, identical on every rank. Uneven is the general path here, not a slow one.

## Under 2-D parallelism

`process_group` takes any subgroup — the sp slice of a tp × sp mesh, with no restriction on which
ranks it contains:

```python
sp_group = mesh["sp"].get_group()
group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)
```

## What will hang you

Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. The first call with a new shape allocates a
window, and that allocation is collective — if one rank takes a branch the others do not, it waits
there. This is the same discipline `torch.distributed` collectives already require.

## Coming from another Ulysses

`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention` and `LongContextAttention` are attention modules, and
sglang's `usp.py` is called from one; this is only the collective, so a port replaces the module
with the two calls above plus your own attention. `scatter_idx` / `gather_idx` map to `mode`, the
`torch.autograd.Function` wrapper is deleted rather than translated, and a caller on `(s, b, n, d)`
still owes a transpose. Call by call: [migration.md](migration.md).

## Checking the machine

```bash
fast-ulysses doctor
```

Prints the build, the devices, and the pairwise NVLink matrix. A group spanning a pair marked `N`
is refused at construction.

188	    # Relative, with the flat name as the fallback: `import fast_ulysses` imports torch, and this
189	    # subcommand has to answer for a torch that is not installed or will not import. Running
190	    # cli.py as a file is the only way to reach here in that state, and there is no package to be
191	    # relative to then.
192	    try:
193	        from ._diagnose import _live, build_meta
194	    except ImportError:
195	        from _diagnose import _live, build_meta
196	
197	    matrix, live, machine = json.loads(_MATRIX.read_text()), _live(), platform.machine()
198	    print(f"running: torch {live['torch']}, cuda {live['cuda']}, {live['python']}, {machine}")
199	
200	    row = _match(matrix, live, machine)
201	    if isinstance(row, str):
202	        print(row)
203	        return 1
204	
205	    # The base version of THIS package: a release publishes one wheel per row, so the row picked
206	    # above only names a file within the release this package came from.
207	    version = str(build_meta().get("VERSION", "")).partition("+")[0]
208	    if not version:
209	        print("_build_meta.py is missing, so the release this package came from cannot be named.")
210	        return 1
211	
212	    torch_abi = ".".join(row["torch"].split(".")[:2])
213	    print(
214	        f"\nrow: torch {torch_abi}, CUDA {row['cuda']}, {live['python']}, {matrix['platform_tag']}"
215	    )
216	    if row.get("pypi"):
217	        print(f"\n  pip install fast-ulysses=={version}\n")
218	        print(
219	            "This is the row PyPI carries, and the only one published without a local\n"
220	            "version: its torch is what a plain `pip install torch` resolves to."
221	        )
222	        return 0
223	
224	    # --find-links, not a constructed asset URL: the filename carries whatever compressed platform
225	    # tag auditwheel emitted, which nothing here can predict, so naming the file would be a guess.
226	    # The release PAGE is useless to pip -- its assets are lazy-loaded and its HTML holds no .whl
227	    # link -- and expanded_assets is the fragment it loads them from, which lists all of them.
228	    print(
229	        f'\n  pip install "fast-ulysses=={version}+{_tag(row)}" \\\n'
230	        f"    --find-links {matrix['find_links'].format(version=version)}\n"
231	    )
232	    pypi_row = next(r for r in matrix["rows"] if r.get("pypi"))
233	    pypi_abi = ".".join(pypi_row["torch"].split(".")[:2])
234	    print(
235	        f"The version has to be written out in full. PEP 440 orders local versions, and\n"
236	        f"{version}+{_tag(pypi_row)} is above every other tag of this release, so both\n"
237	        f"`pip install fast-ulysses` and `fast-ulysses=={version}` resolve to the torch\n"
238	        f"{pypi_abi} wheel -- which declares torch=={pypi_abi}.*, so pip would then move this\n"
239	        f"torch to {pypi_abi} as well. Nothing warns."
240	    )
241	    return 0

244	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
245	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="fast-ulysses")
246	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
247	    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="report the build, the devices, and the NVLink matrix")
248	    sub.add_parser("wheel-url", help="the published wheel for this torch, CUDA, python and arch")
249	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
250	    if args.command == "doctor":
251	        return _doctor()
252	    if args.command == "wheel-url":
253	        return _wheel_url()
254	    parser.error(f"unknown command {args.command}")
255	    return 2

1	# Quick start
2	
3	## Wrapping attention
4	
5	The two calls bracket attention: mode 0 trades the sequence shard for a head shard, mode 1 trades
6	it back.
7	
8	```python
9	import os
10	
11	import torch
12	import torch.distributed as dist
13	from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup
14	
15	dist.init_process_group("nccl")
16	torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
17	ws = dist.get_world_size()
18	
19	group = UlyssesGroup()          # collective; refuses a group that is not NVLink-joined
20	
21	def attention_block(qkv):       # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
22	    qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)      # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
23	    out = attention(qkv)                        # each rank now holds whole sequences
24	    return group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)     # -> (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)
25	```
26	
27	Pack q, k and v into one collective when you can: the last dim is just `3 * head_dim`, and one
28	call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three.
29	
30	## Removing the copy-out
31	
32	The default returns a tensor the call allocated, which costs one flat device-to-device copy out of
33	the window. Give it a symmetric buffer instead and the peers write that buffer directly:
34	
35	```python
36	buf = group.empty_output(qkv, mode=0)     # collective: allocate ONCE, outside the loop
37	for step in range(steps):
38	    y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, out=buf)   # no copy-out; y is buf
39	```
40	
41	`buf` is an ordinary tensor you own. It is overwritten by the next call that uses it, so use one
42	buffer per concurrent call.
43	
44	`out=` gives up the gradient: the result comes back with no `grad_fn` and no `requires_grad`, and
45	nothing raises. Use it in inference and under `torch.no_grad()`; inside a training graph, call
46	without `out=`.
47	
48	## Overlapping with compute
49	
50	The transfer uses no SMs, so it can run underneath compute. Submit it, do the compute, then use the
51	result — the first aten op on it inserts the wait GPU-side.
52	
53	```python
54	y = group.all_to_all_4d_async(qkv, mode=0)   # inference only: raises if qkv requires grad
55	h = some_gemm_chain(other_input)             # runs while the copy engines move qkv
56	y = y.wait()                                 # or just use y; the first op waits by itself
57	```
58	
59	The async form is not differentiable and refuses a grad-requiring input rather than dropping the
60	gradient, so in a training step this is the sync call's job.
61	
62	Wait on, or use, every async result. A dropped one leaves an entry in torch's work registry.
63	
64	## Dropping the sequence padding
65	
66	Sharding a sequence usually means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size and padding the
67	tail, so every rank holds the same length. Those padded tokens then ride through attention and the
68	collective on every layer of every step. Pass the real per-rank lengths instead:
69	
70	```python
71	s = 75827                                    # does not divide by ws
72	seq_splits = [s // ws + (1 if p < s % ws else 0) for p in range(ws)]
73	head_splits = [n_global // ws] * ws
74	
75	y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, seq_splits=seq_splits, head_splits=head_splits)
76	```
77	
78	Both lists or neither, identical on every rank. Uneven is the general path here, not a slow one.
79	
80	## Under 2-D parallelism
81	
82	`process_group` takes any subgroup — the sp slice of a tp × sp mesh, with no restriction on which
83	ranks it contains:
84	
85	```python
86	sp_group = mesh["sp"].get_group()
87	group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)
88	```
89	
90	## What will hang you
91	
92	Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. The first call with a new shape allocates a
93	window, and that allocation is collective — if one rank takes a branch the others do not, it waits
94	there. This is the same discipline `torch.distributed` collectives already require.
95	
96	## Coming from another Ulysses
97	
98	`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention` and `LongContextAttention` are attention modules, and
99	sglang's `usp.py` is called from one; this is only the collective, so a port replaces the module
100	with the two calls above plus your own attention. `scatter_idx` / `gather_idx` map to `mode`, the
101	`torch.autograd.Function` wrapper is deleted rather than translated, and a caller on `(s, b, n, d)`
102	still owes a transpose. Call by call: [migration.md](migration.md).
103	
104	## Checking the machine
105	
106	```bash
107	fast-ulysses doctor
108	```
109	
110	Prints the build, the devices, and the pairwise NVLink matrix. A group spanning a pair marked `N`
111	is refused at construction.

"""Ulysses sequence parallelism around one DiT attention block, forward and backward.

    torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 examples/dit_attention.py

Each rank holds a slice of the sequence and all of the heads. The first all-to-all trades that for
all of the sequence and a slice of the heads, attention runs on whole sequences, and the second
trades back. Both are differentiable, so this is an ordinary module: no autograd.Function wrapper,
no manual backward.

The run checks itself two ways. It compares against the same block with no sequence parallelism at
all -- one rank holding everything -- for both the output and the input gradient. And it prints the
loss over a few optimiser steps, because a collective can be bit-exact in a unit test and still be
wired into the wrong axis of a real module.

The packing matters more than it looks. q, k and v go through ONE collective as a `3 * head_dim`
last axis: one handshake instead of three, for the same bytes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.nn.functional as F

from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

B, S_LOCAL, HEADS_PER_RANK, HEAD_DIM = 1, 512, 4, 128


class UlyssesAttention(torch.nn.Module):
    """One attention block, sequence-parallel over `group`.

    Input and output are both (b, s_local, n_global * head_dim): the shard the caller already has.
    Everything between the two collectives sees whole sequences and a head shard.
    """

    def __init__(self, group: UlyssesGroup, n_global: int, head_dim: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.group, self.n_global, self.head_dim = group, n_global, head_dim
        self.qkv = torch.nn.Linear(n_global * head_dim, 3 * n_global * head_dim, bias=False)
        self.proj = torch.nn.Linear(n_global * head_dim, n_global * head_dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        b, s_local, _ = x.shape

        # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim) -- q, k, v packed into the last axis so the two
        # collectives below stay two collectives.
        qkv = self.qkv(x).view(b, s_local, self.n_global, 3 * self.head_dim)

        # mode 0: sequence shard -> head shard. Differentiable; its backward is mode 1.
        qkv = self.group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)  # (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)

        q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
        # SDPA wants (b, heads, s, d).
        attn = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
        ).transpose(1, 2)  # (b, s_global, n_local, head_dim)

        # mode 1: back to a sequence shard, all heads. Its backward is mode 0.
        attn = self.group.all_to_all_4d(attn.contiguous(), mode=1)
        return self.proj(attn.reshape(b, s_local, self.n_global * self.head_dim))


def reference(module: UlyssesAttention, x_global: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The same block with no sequence parallelism: one rank, whole sequence, all heads."""
    b, s, _ = x_global.shape
    qkv = module.qkv(x_global).view(b, s, module.n_global, 3 * module.head_dim)
    q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
    attn = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
        q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
    ).transpose(1, 2)
    return module.proj(attn.reshape(b, s, module.n_global * module.head_dim))


def main() -> None:
    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
    rank, ws = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", rank)))

15	The packing matters more than it looks. q, k and v go through ONE collective as a `3 * head_dim`
16	last axis: one handshake instead of three, for the same bytes.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import os
22	
23	import torch
24	import torch.distributed as dist
25	import torch.nn.functional as F
26	
27	from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup
28	
29	B, S_LOCAL, HEADS_PER_RANK, HEAD_DIM = 1, 512, 4, 128
30	
31	
32	class UlyssesAttention(torch.nn.Module):
33	    """One attention block, sequence-parallel over `group`.
34	
35	    Input and output are both (b, s_local, n_global * head_dim): the shard the caller already has.
36	    Everything between the two collectives sees whole sequences and a head shard.
37	    """
38	
39	    def __init__(self, group: UlyssesGroup, n_global: int, head_dim: int) -> None:
40	        super().__init__()
41	        self.group, self.n_global, self.head_dim = group, n_global, head_dim
42	        self.qkv = torch.nn.Linear(n_global * head_dim, 3 * n_global * head_dim, bias=False)
43	        self.proj = torch.nn.Linear(n_global * head_dim, n_global * head_dim, bias=False)
44	
45	    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
46	        b, s_local, _ = x.shape
47	
48	        # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim) -- q, k, v packed into the last axis so the two
49	        # collectives below stay two collectives.
50	        qkv = self.qkv(x).view(b, s_local, self.n_global, 3 * self.head_dim)
51	
52	        # mode 0: sequence shard -> head shard. Differentiable; its backward is mode 1.
53	        qkv = self.group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)  # (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
54	
55	        q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
56	        # SDPA wants (b, heads, s, d).
57	        attn = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
58	            q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
59	        ).transpose(1, 2)  # (b, s_global, n_local, head_dim)
60	
61	        # mode 1: back to a sequence shard, all heads. Its backward is mode 0.
62	        attn = self.group.all_to_all_4d(attn.contiguous(), mode=1)
63	        return self.proj(attn.reshape(b, s_local, self.n_global * self.head_dim))
64	
65	
66	def reference(module: UlyssesAttention, x_global: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
67	    """The same block with no sequence parallelism: one rank, whole sequence, all heads."""
68	    b, s, _ = x_global.shape
69	    qkv = module.qkv(x_global).view(b, s, module.n_global, 3 * module.head_dim)
70	    q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
71	    attn = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
72	        q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
73	    ).transpose(1, 2)
74	    return module.proj(attn.reshape(b, s, module.n_global * module.head_dim))
75	
76	
77	def main() -> None:
78	    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
79	    rank, ws = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
80	    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", rank)))

# 安装、构建与第一次运行

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 看一眼当前环境（torch 版本、CUDA 版本、Python 版本、GPU 架构），就知道该装哪个 wheel——或者为什么必须源码构建。
2. 用 `FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH=<本机架构> pip install -e . --no-build-isolation` 完成一次快速源码构建，并能解释 `--no-build-isolation` 为什么是必需的而不是习惯。
3. 用 `torchrun` 跑通 README 的 quickstart 脚本和 `examples/dit_attention.py`，包括只有一张卡（或零张卡）时如何降级运行、哪些行为在 `world_size=1` 时仍然成立。
4. 读懂 `fast-ulysses doctor` 的三段输出（构建信息、设备列表、NVLink 矩阵），并据此判断这台机器能不能跑这个算子。

本讲是纯「工程上手」讲：不改任何算法代码，只解决「让它在你机器上跑起来」这件事。

## 2. 前置知识

- **wheel 与 ABI**：Python 的 wheel 是预编译的二进制包。包含 C++/CUDA 扩展的 wheel 不是「一个 Linux 包到处能跑」——它编译时链接的头文件、符号和数据结构布局，必须与运行时的环境一致。这种一致性约束统称 ABI（Application Binary Interface）。
- **torch 的版本坐标**：一个 torch 安装由两个数字定位——`torch.__version__`（如 `2.11.0`）和 `torch.version.cuda`（如 `12.8`）。前者的 **minor**（`2.11` 中的 `11`）决定 C++ ABI，后者的 **major**（`12`）决定链接哪份 `libcudart`。fast-ulysses 的 wheel 就是按「torch minor × CUDA major」这两个轴发布的。
- **GPU 架构（compute capability）**：NVIDIA GPU 按架构编号，如 H100 是 `sm_90`、A100 是 `sm_80`、B200 是 `sm_100`。CUDA 扩展编译时要显式列出为哪些架构生成代码；列得越多编译越慢。用 `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)` 可以读出本机卡的 `major`/`minor`。
- **torchrun**：PyTorch 自带的分布式启动器。`torchrun --nproc_per_node=N script.py` 会启动 N 个进程，每个进程拿到不同的 `RANK` / `LOCAL_RANK` 环境变量，你需要在脚本里 `torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))` 把每个进程绑到自己的卡。
- **PEP 440 local version**：Python 包版本可以带「本地标签」，写成 `0.2.0+torch210cu128` 这种 `版本+标签` 的形式。pip 在比较版本时会**给这些标签排序**——这正是本讲会反复踩到的一个坑的根源（见 4.1.3）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [README.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md) | 项目门面：Quick start 脚本、Install 一节的四条命令、Testing 命令 |
| [docs/install.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md) | 安装的权威文档：wheel 行表、索引选择、PEP 440 陷阱、构建变量表、导入失败排查 |
| [setup.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/setup.py) | 源码构建入口：调用 CMake、生成 `_build_meta.py`、按内存限制并行度 |
| [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/pyproject.toml) | 包元数据：`fast-ulysses` 命令行入口、包目录布局、pytest 配置 |
| [python/fast_ulysses/cli.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/cli.py) | `doctor` 与 `wheel-url` 两个子命令的实现 |
| [python/fast_ulysses/__init__.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/__init__.py) | 包导入：先加载 torch 再 dlopen `_C`，失败时转成诊断报告 |
| [examples/dit_attention.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py) | 第一个「真实」示例：序列并行注意力块，前向 + 反向 + 自校验 |
| [src/barrier.cu](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/barrier.cu) | 标志位屏障实现；本讲只看它 `world_size == 1` 时直接返回这一个事实 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 wheel 选择：按「torch minor × CUDA major」对号入座

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

fast-ulysses 的核心是一个名为 `_C` 的 C++/CUDA 扩展（`.so` 文件）。这个扩展里嵌入了 torch 内部的 C++ 成分——`c10d::Work` 虚表、pybind11 模块、`TORCH_LIBRARY` 算子注册。torch 每升一个 minor（2.10 → 2.11），这些内部结构就可能变化，扩展立刻无法加载。CUDA major（12 → 13）则决定扩展链接的是 `libcudart.so.12` 还是 `libcudart.so.13`。所以 wheel 必须精确匹配 **torch 的 minor** 和 **CUDA 的 major**，这两条合起来就是发布矩阵的「行」。

一个发布是 36 个 wheel：8 个（torch minor × CUDA major）行 × 4 个 CPython 版本，再加 4 个去掉本地标签、发到 PyPI 的 wheel。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

确定自己该装哪个 wheel 的流程：

1. 查询环境三元组：torch 版本、torch 的 CUDA 版本、Python 版本。
2. 在行表里找到（torch minor, CUDA major）对应的标签，如 `torch211cu128`。
3. 按下面的优先级选安装方式：
   - 想让 pip 自动解析 → 用 `whl/cu12` 或 `whl/cu13` 总索引；
   - 同一条命令里还要从 PyPI 装别的东西 → 用 `whl/<tag>` 单行索引；
   - 想要文件本身 → `fast-ulysses wheel-url` 打印的 `--find-links` 命令（版本必须写全）；
   - 你的 torch 不在表里 → 源码构建（4.2）。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**第一步：查环境。** 文档给出的这条命令一次打全三个坐标：

```bash
python -c "import sys,torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, sys.version_info[:2])"
```

出处：[docs/install.md:L22-L24](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L22-L24)——用当前 torch 的实际输出去查下面这张表。

**第二步：查行表。** 8 个行标签覆盖 torch 2.10–2.13 × CUDA 12/13：

> | your torch | torch's CUDA | wheel tag |
> |---|---|---|
> | 2.10.x | 12.x | `torch210cu128` |
> | … | … | … |
> | 2.13.x | 13.x | `torch213cu130` |

出处：[docs/install.md:L26-L35](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L26-L35)。表中行标签就是 wheel 的 PEP 440 本地版本（`fast_ulysses-0.2.0+torch210cu128-cp312-…`）。

**第三步：选索引。** README 的 Install 一节给出首选命令：

```bash
pip install fast-ulysses --index-url https://triple-mu.github.io/fast-ulysses/whl/cu13/   # or cu12
```

出处：[README.md:L131-L138](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L131-L138)。关键机制在 [docs/install.md:L51-L54](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L51-L54)：这个索引**只有 fast-ulysses 没有别的包**，所以 pip 无法靠安装一个新 torch 来满足最高候选者，只能一路回退到「`Requires-Dist: torch==2.11.*` 恰好被你已装的 torch 满足」的那一行。torch minor 不靠你选，靠这个回退解析。CUDA major 靠 URL 选（`cu12` / `cu13`），因为 wheel 元数据里不记录 CUDA 版本——这与 `download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128` 的目录组织是同一个道理（[docs/install.md:L46-L49](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L46-L49)）。

**两个必须知道的坑：**

- **PyPI 坑**：PyPI 不接受带本地标签的版本，所以 PyPI 上只有 `torch213cu130` 一行（钉死 `torch==2.13.*`）。在任何其他 torch 上，裸的 `pip install fast-ulysses` **不会报错**——pip 会直接把你的 torch 升级到 2.13（一份和你所选不同的 CUDA 构建），并且把它报告成一次普通的依赖解析。见 [docs/install.md:L114-L124](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L114-L124) 与 [README.md:L146-L147](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L146-L147)。同理，不要 `--extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple`——这等于亲手把 torch 交还给 pip（[docs/install.md:L71-L73](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L71-L73)）。
- **PEP 440 排序坑**：本地标签按段比较，而不带标签的 `==0.2.0` 会**完全忽略**标签。于是在任何持有多个行的文件集合（`--find-links`、wheelhouse 目录）上，不带标签的要求永远解析到最高的 `+torch213cu130`，与你装了什么 torch 无关、且无任何警告（[docs/install.md:L127-L145](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L127-L145)）。所以用 `--find-links` 时版本必须写全：`pip install "fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu128" --find-links …`。

**让工具替你查：`wheel-url` 子命令。** 它读取当前环境的 torch/CUDA/Python/机器架构，按 machine → python → torch minor → CUDA major 的顺序匹配，打印出写全版本的安装命令：

出处：[python/fast_ulysses/cli.py:L187-L241](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/cli.py#L187-L241)。匹配顺序（machine → python → torch → CUDA）的实现和每一步失败时的提示语在 [cli.py:L130-L184](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/cli.py#L130-L184)；注意它是**故意只匹配 CUDA major** 的，因为扩展只从 toolkit 链接 `libcudart.so.<major>`（[cli.py:L133-L137](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/cli.py#L133-L137) 的 docstring）。没有任何 wheel 匹配时，每条提示语最后都落在同一条出路——源码构建（[cli.py:L113-L115](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/cli.py#L113-L115)）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：同事在 torch 2.11 + CUDA 12.8 的环境里执行了 `pip install fast-ulysses --find-links ./wheelhouse`（wheelhouse 里有全部 36 个 wheel），结果 `import fast_ulysses` 报 `undefined symbol: _ZN3c10...`。为什么？

**答案**：不带标签的要求在 PEP 440 下忽略本地版本并取最高者，于是装上了 `+torch213cu130`，而它嵌的是 torch 2.13 的 C++ ABI，与已装的 torch 2.11 不匹配，dlopen 时出现 undefined symbol。修复：`pip uninstall -y fast-ulysses` 后用写全标签的 `pip install "fast-ulysses==0.2.1+torch211cu128" --find-links ./wheelhouse`（排查流程见 [docs/install.md:L187-L213](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L187-L213)）。

**练习 2**：为什么 `whl/cu13` 索引不需要你在版本里写 `+torchXXXcu130` 标签，而 `--find-links` 需要？

**答案**：索引里只有 fast-ulysses 一个项目，pip 装不了新 torch，只能回退到 `Requires-Dist: torch==<你的minor>.*` 被现有 torch 满足的那一行——torch minor 由依赖解析决定。而 `--find-links`/多索引场景下 pip 会对所有候选取最高版本，最高标签永远是 `torch213cu130`，必须写全标签才能钉住行（[docs/install.md:L51-L54](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L51-L54) 与 [L147-L152](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L147-L152)）。

**练习 3**：一个全新环境（没装 torch）执行 `pip install fast-ulysses --index-url https://triple-mu.github.io/fast-ulysses/whl/cu13/` 会发生什么？这是 bug 吗？

**答案**：没有任何候选者的 torch 钉能被满足，pip 以 `ResolutionImpossible` 结束并列出它试过的每一行。这是**有意的失败**——这套索引的设计原则就是「不替你解析 torch」（[docs/install.md:L56-L69](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L56-L69)）；先 `pip install torch` 即可。

### 4.2 源码构建：`--no-build-isolation` 与 `FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH`

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

当你的 torch 不在 8 个发布行里、或者你要改 C++/CUDA 源码做开发，就需要源码构建。它不是「备胎」：本学习手册后面每一讲带你改代码观察行为，用的都是 `pip install -e .`（可编辑安装）这条路。

源码构建有两个本项目特有的关键点：

- **`--no-build-isolation` 是硬性要求**。pip 默认在隔离的临时环境里跑构建，那个环境没有你的 torch；而 fast-ulysses 的构建**必须 import 你将要链接的那份 torch**（读它的版本、让 CMake 定位 libtorch）。这不是惯例，是设计约束——违反时构建直接失败并打印修复指引，而不是抛 traceback。
- **默认编译 4 个架构（`80;90;100;120`），很慢；用 `FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH` 只编本机架构可以快几倍**。每个架构一次独立的设备端编译过程，nvcc 还会让它们并行跑，内存消耗也按架构数放大。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`pip install -e . --no-build-isolation` 触发的链条：

```text
pip（不隔离，用当前环境）
  └─ setup.py: CMakeBuild.build_extension
       ├─ 读取 FAST_ULYSSES_CUDA_ARCH（默认 "80;90;100;120"）
       ├─ 转写成 torch 的点分形式 → TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST（90 → "9.0"）
       ├─ cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=…  （configure）
       ├─ cmake --build build -jN                           （N 由内存预算决定）
       └─ 生成 fast_ulysses/_build_meta.py（构建事实快照）
```

并行作业数 \(N\) 不跟随 CPU 核数，而是按内存预算：每个 nvcc 作业对每个架构各跑一个设备端 pass，峰值并发是「作业数 × 架构数」，按每个 pass 约 3 GiB 预算：

\[
N \;=\; \max\!\Big(1,\ \min\big(\text{cpus},\ \big\lfloor \mathrm{MemAvail}_{\mathrm{GiB}} \,/\, (3.0 \cdot n_{\mathrm{arch}}) \big\rfloor\big)\Big)
\]

`CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL` 环境变量可以越过这个推导。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**pyproject.toml 的构建声明与命令行入口：**

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
...
[project.scripts]
fast-ulysses = "fast_ulysses.cli:main"
```

出处：[pyproject.toml:L1-L3](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/pyproject.toml#L1-L3) 与 [pyproject.toml:L20-L21](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/pyproject.toml#L20-L21)。注意 `version` 和 `dependencies` 是 `dynamic` 的（[pyproject.toml:L12](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/pyproject.toml#L12)）——都由 setup.py 在构建时从真实 torch 推导。第二行就是 `fast-ulysses doctor` / `fast-ulysses wheel-url` 这两个命令的来源。包本体在 `python/` 下（[pyproject.toml:L29-L34](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/pyproject.toml#L29-L34)），`wheel_matrix.json` 作为包数据一起安装。

**`--no-build-isolation` 的强制与解释**——`_requires()` 里的这段注释是全项目对这个问题最完整的论证：

```python
def _requires() -> list[str]:
    """... Reading it needs the torch this will link against, so the build cannot run under pip's
    build isolation -- and torch cannot be declared a build requirement either, because pip
    would then install its own copy into the isolated environment and the extension would link
    that one instead of the user's. Turn the bare ModuleNotFoundError into the instruction."""
    try:
        import torch
    except ImportError:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "fast-ulysses builds against the torch already installed in the target environment, "
            "so it cannot be built under pip's build isolation.\n"
            ...
```
